safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not state that the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the headache is still present can blur the clinical picture (ongoing vs resolved), which may affect assessment of acuity and follow-up urgency. However, it is unlikely by itself to directly change immediate management in this context.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of neck stiffness (or denial of it) in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Neck stiffness is a key red-flag feature for meningitis/SAH; omitting a documented denial can weaken safety-netting and risk stratification for potentially time-critical conditions. This could delay escalation if a clinician later assumes the symptom was not assessed.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of fever (or denial of it) in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is an important red-flag symptom in headache (infection/meningitis); failing to document its absence reduces confidence that serious causes were considered. This can lead to missed or delayed recognition of higher-risk presentations.
